alignments.note: MACULA reads the prefix as the interrogative הֲ (Ti), not the article, and the ASV writes no question at all here — neither a fronted auxiliary nor inversion — so the particle is unrepresented under rule 17's inversion-alone sentence. The margin (*The Hebrew as pointed reads Is it fit to say to a king...*) records the interrogative reading the printed text declines, and was read and set aside under rule 38. The competing reading treats the prefix as the substantival article and gives it *Him that* under rule 41, but rule 41 governs the article הַ and rule 39 makes the morphology what is read.

The infinitive stands substantivally with no article morpheme present, so the supplied *Him that* joins its own unit under rule 46, headed on the word carrying the lexeme rather than on the supplied pronoun. Rule 11's ordering settles it: no source function morpheme's sense is carried by *Him that*, so the substantive takes it as a supplied helper.
Supplied indefinite article joins the noun (rule 15).
Verbless clause: the construction-supplied copula joins the predicate (rule 20).
Second verbless predicate takes its copula (rule 20).
Supplied subject pronoun in a verbless clause whose predicate morpheme takes only the copula (rule 20).
No conjunction morpheme stands in the clause for the supplied *Or* (rule 14's last sentence).
Supplied subject pronoun, as in the first quoted clause (rule 20).

review_notes: Corrected: the accepted alignment gave *Him that* to s001 under rule 41's substantival article, but s001 is tagged Ti (the interrogative הֲ), and rule 39 makes the morphology what is read. The particle is unrepresented because the ASV renders no question, and *Him that* joins the anarthrous substantive אֲמֹר under rule 46, moving the head from the supplied pronoun to the lexeme-bearing *saith*.
Every ASV italic here corroborates rather than decides (rule 7); the two copulas stay with their predicates under rule 20 while the supplied subjects are added.
